parts.visual:
After 10 years of grueling work, the founders stand on the balcony of the New York Stock Exchange and ring the opening bell. Confetti falls. Their private startup is now a public corporation. Millions of normal people can now buy a piece of their company on a smartphone app. Overnight, the founders and early investors become billionaires on paper.

The Exit:
1. The IPO: An Initial Public Offering is the process of offering shares of a private corporation to the public in a new stock issuance. It is the ultimate 'Exit Event' for a startup.
2. The Trade-off: Going public gives the company massive capital and prestige, but it comes with a brutal curse. The CEO is now legally required to report profits every 90 days to Wall Street, destroying long-term thinking.
parts.audio: An IPO is not the finish line; it is just a different, much louder starting line. You trade the quiet pressure of five venture capitalists for the screaming, chaotic pressure of ten million public shareholders who want their stock to go up every single day.

questions.question: Why do Venture Capitalists force founders to eventually IPO or sell the company?
options: The Liquidity Mandate. VCs invest money on behalf of pension funds and billionaires. A VC fund has a strict 10-year lifespan. If the startup remains private forever, the stock is 'illiquid' (it cannot be sold for cash), and the VC cannot return cash to their own investors.
Because public companies have better logos.
questions.correct_answer: The Liquidity Mandate. VCs invest money on behalf of pension funds and billionaires. A VC fund has a strict 10-year lifespan. If the startup remains private forever, the stock is 'illiquid' (it cannot be sold for cash), and the VC cannot return cash to their own investors.
questions.explanation: Paper billions are useless until an exit event turns them into liquid cash.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO who just went public. What is the '90-Day Treadmill'?
questions.tts_text: When we were private, I could spend $50 million on a secret project that wouldn't make money for 3 years. Now that we are public, I have to release an 'Earnings Report' every quarter. If profits drop for even one quarter, the stock crashes and I get fired.
options: Quarterly Capitalism. Public markets demand short-term, predictable profits every 90 days. This creates immense pressure on the CEO to cut R&D spending and artificially boost short-term revenue just to keep Wall Street analysts happy.
questions.correct_answer: Quarterly Capitalism. Public markets demand short-term, predictable profits every 90 days. This creates immense pressure on the CEO to cut R&D spending and artificially boost short-term revenue just to keep Wall Street analysts happy.

questions.question: What is a 'Lock-Up Period' after an IPO?
options: When the CEO goes to jail.

A legal rule (usually 180 days) preventing founders and early employees from selling their stock immediately on IPO day. This stops insiders from instantly cashing out and crashing the stock price before normal public investors have a chance to trade.
questions.correct_answer: A legal rule (usually 180 days) preventing founders and early employees from selling their stock immediately on IPO day. This stops insiders from instantly cashing out and crashing the stock price before normal public investors have a chance to trade.
questions.explanation: You are rich on paper today, but you can't buy the Ferrari for 6 months.

questions.question: What role does an 'Investment Bank' (like Goldman Sachs) play in an IPO?
options: They are the Underwriters. They manage the incredibly complex legal paperwork, determine the initial price of the stock, and travel the world pitching the stock to massive institutional buyers (like mutual funds) before the bell rings.
questions.correct_answer: They are the Underwriters. They manage the incredibly complex legal paperwork, determine the initial price of the stock, and travel the world pitching the stock to massive institutional buyers (like mutual funds) before the bell rings.
questions.explanation: They are the expensive tour guides to Wall Street.

pairs.match: Initial Public Offering; when a private startup sells shares to the public
The ability to easily convert startup stock shares into actual cash
The brutal 90-day cycle of reporting profits to Wall Street
The 6-month delay before founders are legally allowed to sell their stock
